articles.title: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir peeks into the lost theatre of diplomacy
articles.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging – A Journey of Love , has made unique contributions to India’s diplomatic lore that exhaustive discussions of the book so far in India and abroad have ignored. Without the author’s anecdotes from extensive travels with two prime ministers from her family, and later as Congress president, these and many related episodes from Indian diplomacy may have gone to the grave. Gandhi’s narrations in the book are matter-of-fact sequences, nothing like tales chronicled by professional diplomats from time to time, a growing trend in India. Her best story, told in innocence, as she admits, concerns Nancy Reagan, wife of Ronald Reagan, the United States President during Rajiv Gandhi’s first visit to Washington as Prime Minister. “Whatever I wore for each occasion would be matched by Mrs. Reagan in the same colours.” The author calls it the “Mystery of the Wardrobe.” It happened on every occasion on every day of the Gandhi couple’s stay in Washington. Researching for her memoir, the author discovered that “it was the same story” when Indira Gandhi visited the US in 1982. “Mrs. Reagan’s outfits mostly matched perfectly in shade Mrs. Gandhi’s.” The memoir says the exercise was pointless, but was the White House sending a message? That their hosts had so deeply penetrated the Indian delegation as to know what the visiting prime minister’s spouse — and the predecessor prime minister herself three years earlier — would be wearing on each occasion? She belonged to my father, my father belonged to her: Rahul Gandhi on Sonia-Rajiv bond I have my own mystery of the Indian VVIP wardrobe, which was solved by one of the dramatis personae in the episode many years after it surfaced. In 1981, when Indira Gandhi visited the United Arab Emirates, I noticed that every evening, the prime minister and Indira Mansingh, wife of the then Indian ambassador to the UAE, wore exactly the same saris. Indira Gandhi noticed it first in Abu Dhabi, but merely gave Mansingh a curious look. When the same thing happened in Dubai the next day with another set of saris, Indira Gandhi told the diplomat’s spouse: “Once is OK. Twice is too much.” Mansingh told me that the prime minister’s confidante and social secretary, Usha Bhagat, used to order Indira Gandhi’s saris. Bhagat and Mansingh were friends. So, on a few occasions, Bhagat ordered the same sari for Mansingh too. No one foresaw the faux pas that the prime minister and the ambassador’s wife would wear identical saris not once, but twice, in each other’s presence. Sonia Gandhi’s second-best story is about former French President Nicolas Sarkozy, who was nudged by the prudish Indian side not to bring his stunning singer-songwriter girlfriend, Carla Bruni, on a visit in 2008 because they were an unmarried couple. Unaffected by any such hypocrisy, Vice President Mohammad Ansari’s wife, Salma Ansari, began quizzing Sarkozy about Bruni at the Rashtrapati Bhavan banquet for the visiting French head of state. “Was he missing her? Was he going to get married? Had the date been decided?...” Good-naturedly, Sarkozy answered all of her questions. “Sarkozy seemed even eager to share details of his love life,” writes Sonia Gandhi. By the time Sarkozy visited India again, he was married to Bruni and brought her along. “All eyes were on her” wherever she went with her husband. The Ansaris were in Abu Dhabi when I went to live in the UAE in 1978. Salma Ansari was always unconventional in her own charming way. When the Vice President and Second Lady called on Fidel Castro at his sickbed, it was a rare meeting allowed by Cuban doctors as Castro was recovering from cancer. Salma Ansari cheekily asked Castro at that meeting about the women in his life and wanted to know if he was always a hit with women. According to C Rajasekhar, India’s then Ambassador in Havana, Castro was silent for a long time, dreamy and wistful. Then he smiled and said: “When I was young, I was lucky. Yes, I was very lucky.” Sonia Gandhi says about US President Bill Clinton that the Monica Lewinsky scandal had subsided somewhat by the time Clinton visited India in 2000, “but old habits die hard. At the reception held by Prime Minister Vajpayee in his honour, I noticed him (Clinton) every now and then surreptitiously sizing up the more striking women present.” I have a postscript to this story. When Clinton visited Hyderabad as part of his itinerary, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu, assigned film actress Jayaprada, then a Telugu Desam MP, to accompany the president everywhere in Hyderabad like a minister-in-waiting. Clinton was most pleased. Senior diplomat T P Sreenivasan, who was present, told me that when Jayaprada took leave of Clinton, the president was visibly disappointed and asked the MP: “Oh! You are not going with me to Mumbai?” Sonia Gandhi’s constructive criticism of Indian official banquets and other arrangements for visiting foreign leaders — especially Rashtrapati Bhavan banquets — is something I wholeheartedly share from my many decades of covering those in a professional capacity. It has only got worse in recent years. Some leaders, most notably Chinese President Xi Jinping in September, choose to skip those dinners, courteously pleading tiredness at the end of long working days. With her feminine touch fused with Indian and European upbringing, it is tempting to think what changes Sonia Gandhi would have made if she had become president, having once renounced prime minstership. K P Nayar has extensively covered West Asia and reported from Washington as a foreign correspondent for 15 years. Disclaimer: The views expressed above are the author's own. Supreme Court declines urgent listing of plea seeking recall of CEC Act reference order
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to urgently list an application seeking recall of a two-judge bench order that referred the question related to validity of 2023 law on appointment of Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners for adjudication before the Constitution bench. Advocate Prashant Bhushan mentioned the matter before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. He sought that the recall plea be placed before the same two-judge bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma, which had ordered the reference. The application cited an alleged conflict of interest, stating that Justice Sharma’s son appears as standing counsel for the Election Commission of India. Supreme Court declines plea for separate hearing on recall of split verdict in ECs' appointment case Pointing to Justice Sharma’s retirement at the end of next week, Bhushan pressed for an urgent listing. Justice Sharma is to superannuate on November 29, 2026. Chief Justice Kant, however, directed him to raise the issue before the five-judge Constitution bench when the matter is taken up. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, also on the bench, observed that the Constitution bench could itself examine the validity of the reference. Bhushan contended that the reference had arisen primarily because of Justice Sharma’s dissent. “If Justice Sharma had not dissented, the matter would not have been referred to the Constitution bench,” he submitted. The Chief Justice noted that Justice Datta had ultimately concurred with the reference. “My role was only to constitute the bench,” he said.Bhushan reiterated that the recall application should go back to the original two-judge bench and sought its listing next week, warning that Justice Sharma’s impending retirement could affect its consideration. The Chief Justice declined the request. “You can raise it before the bench when the matter comes. The presiding judge is there in any case,” he said. The recall plea challenges the two-judge bench’s decision to refer the challenge to the 2023 Act governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners. On September 23, 2026, a bench of Justices Datta and Sharma rendered a split view on issue of reference to the larger bench. The original pleas challenged Sections 7 and 8 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 which provided for a selection committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition and a Cabinet Minister. Justice Datta held that no reference to a larger bench was required, while Justice Sharma observed that a substantial question of constitutional law arose under Article 145(3). The matter was ultimately placed before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant for consideration by a Constitution Bench to avoid further delay.

Sharad further shared that he plans to meet SRK’s son and filmmaker Aryan Khan . In an interview with Navbharat Times , Sharad revisited his telephonic conversation with SRK. He said his Josh co-star checked in on his well-being and encouraged him to take on whatever work he wished. " SRK said, Do whatever you like and wish to do; I am ready to help you in any way ," said Sharad. He also added that he will soon be meeting Aryan Khan, who recently made his directorial debut with Netflix’s The Ba*ds of Bollywood (2025). In the movie, he played Prakash, the antagonist opposite SRK’s character, Max. Calling him a " man of immense stature and a self-assured actor ," Sharad said that he used to help Shah Rukh Khan whenever he got stuck on a dialogue. Even in scenes where their characters clashed, they both wanted to make a good film. SRK joins a growing list of Bollywood celebrities and industry bodies coming forward to support Sharad Kapoor in these difficult times. Earlier this week, Sonu Sood met with him and arranged for a medical team and healthcare facility in Karjat, near Mumbai, to treat his leg injury, while Salman Khan offered financial aid and assured him of his backing. Meanwhile, the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) publicly urged filmmakers to cast Sharad, and colleagues including Javed Akhtar, Rajpal Yadav and Armaan Kohli also called to check on him. Sharad Kapoor, 50, recently sparked widespread concern online after a video surfaced showing him parting with his four pet dogs and sending them to a care centre due to his declining health and poor living conditions. Opening up about his struggles, Sharad spoke about depression, the emotional toll of past allegations and a severe leg injury sustained while playing football in Barcelona, which now requires him to use a walker. He further said that he wanted to get back on set rather than seek financial handouts. " Money is not the issue. The only issue is I am just looking forward to start work again ," he said in his appeal. Sharad made his debut in 1994 with Mera Pyara Bharat and appeared in films such as Tamanna, LOC Kargil, Lakshya and Jai Ho . He is now reportedly travelling to Karjat for medical treatment and hopes to recover in time to resume work in January 2027.

articles.title: Supreme Court declines plea for separate hearing on recall of split verdict in ECs' appointment case
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday declined a submission to separately list a plea seeking recall of a split verdict delivered by a two-judge bench on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) should be referred to a larger bench. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the recall application, as well as any challenge to the reference order, could be considered by the five-judge Constitution bench already constituted to hear the batch of petitions challenging the validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. The CJI also said the five-judge bench could consider the recall application even after the retirement of one of the judges who delivered the split verdict. 'We will take a call': Supreme Court to examine plea for recall of split verdict on law governing appointment of CEC, ECs Bhushan said that the recall application should be listed before the original bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma, which delivered the split verdict on September 23. He pointed out that Justice Sharma was due to retire next week. Bhushan further said that Justice Sharma had a conflict of interest and, therefore, the application seeking recall of the verdict ought to be heard by the same bench. When the CJI suggested that the reference bench could consider the application, Bhushan said the reference order itself was recalled on the ground of an alleged conflict of interest. However, the CJI said that the issue could be raised before the five-judge Constitution bench, which has been constituted for final adjudication of the constitutional challenge to the 2023 law. The development follows a split verdict delivered on September 23 by Justices Datta and Sharma on whether the petitions challenging the 2023 law warranted consideration by a larger bench. The main objection was the exclusion of the CJI from the panel to select the CEC and ECs. The panel now includes the prime minister, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha and a cabinet minister. While Justice Datta was of the view that the challenge could be adjudicated by a two-judge bench, Justice Sharma favoured a reference to a five-judge Constitution bench, considering the significant constitutional questions involved.

articles.title: Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu's pleas on release of Cauvery water
articles.summary: New Delhi: In a setback to Tamil Nadu , the Supreme Court on Friday dismissed the state’s applications seeking directions to Karnataka to release around 11 thousand million cubic feet (TMC) of Cauvery water to make up for the shortfall this year. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Singh pronounced the order in open court, rejecting two applications filed by Tamil Nadu. “There were two applications. Both the applications are dismissed” the bench said. The court also took note of a third application filed by Tamil Nadu on the same day. Cauvery water row: Supreme Court asks Tamil Nadu to approach CWMA with grievances “You have filed another application today. The state of Tamil Nadu has a lot of funds,” Justice Nath observed in a lighter vein, before adjourning the third application. On the joint request of counsel for both States, it was listed after one week. Tamil Nadu had approached the apex court alleging that Karnataka had failed to release the water due to it, in violation of the Supreme Court’s earlier judgement. The State pointed out that although the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) meet every 15 days, they had not ordered the release of the outstanding quantity. The State submitted that this had been a year of insufficient rainfall. It said Karnataka owed Tamil Nadu 11 TMC of water since July and urged that the deficit be made good by releasing an additional 1 TMC per day to protect standing crops. According to the Supreme Court’s formula, Karnataka is required to release 177 TMC to Tamil Nadu in a normal year; in a distress year the quantity is reduced proportionately. Karnataka to move Supreme Court against order to release 6,000 cusecs Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu Even after accounting for the reduced allocation, a shortfall of 11 TMC remained at the Billigundulu inter-state border measuring point as of early October, Tamil Nadu contended. Karnataka countered that several districts in the State were facing drought and that irrigation allocations had already been cut. It argued that Tamil Nadu would benefit from the forthcoming northeast monsoon while Karnataka would not, and that the CWMA and CWRC were regularly monitoring the situation. There was therefore no need for court intervention, it submitted. The court had reserved its order on October 12 on Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking immediate release of the backlog of about 11 TMC at the rate of 1.3 TMC per day over 10 days at Billigundulu.

articles.title: Indian origin grandmother's deportation by ICE prompts new legislation in US Congress
articles.summary: Washington: A Sikh grandmother’s deportation to India after three decades of stay in the US has prompted four California lawmakers to introduce a bill in the US Congress to protect long-term immigrant residents. The Protect Our Neighbours Act, introduced by Congressman John Garamendi, draws inspiration from the deportation of Harjit Kaur, a resident of the San Francisco Bay Area, by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) last year. The draft legislation has also received support from representatives Lateefah Simon, Zoe Lofgren, and Juan Vargas. “The Protect Our Neighbours Act would provide people, like Ms. Kaur who worked in my district for decades, with a fair opportunity to move beyond a final order of removal and continue building futures here in the US where they have made their homes and families,” Simon said. Garamendi said nearly one year ago, ICE cruelly detained and deported Kaur, a 73-year-old grandmother with no criminal record — who faithfully reported to ICE every six months for more than 13 years. ICE deportation flight carrying Iranians turns back and lands in Arizona Her cruel and unreasonable detention and deportation is just one more example of the thousands of individuals across the country whose lives and families have been upended by President Donald Trump’s ICE, Garamendi said. According to the American Immigration Council, roughly 1.19 million people with removal orders remain in the US, many having spent years building lives, raising families, and working here. Under President Trump, the Department of Homeland Security and ICE have aggressively pursued individuals with final removal orders, regardless of how long the case had been deferred, putting long-term residents who have routinely complied with check-ins at renewed risk of detention and deportation. The bill seeks to make final removal orders expire 10 years after issuance. An immigration judge could renew an expired order at the Homeland Security Secretary’s request, but only with clear and convincing evidence of significant reasons for the delay unrelated to administrative or funding problems, and new evidence establishing that renewal served the public interest. People with expired, unrenewed orders could seek lawful status for which they qualify after at least 10 years’ continuous US presence, provided they had no conviction for an offence punishable by more than a year in prison. Renewal would be barred while that petition was pending. A separate provision would allow discretionary permanent residence for certain people physically present in the US with longstanding orders based on specified immigration grounds.

articles.title: Kerala police bring back absconding murder accused from Dubai after 18 years
articles.summary: A man who was absconding for nearly 18 years in a murder case in Kerala’s Thrissur was brought back to India from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and arrested with the assistance of Interpol. The accused, Rakesh Unnikochan (46), also identified as Raghesh Unnikochan in the Central Bureau of Investigation’s (CBI) statement, is the third accused in the murder of Dhanesh, a resident of Thirumangalam in Engandiyur, Thrissur. He was apprehended in Dubai following the issuance of an Interpol Red Corner Notice (RCN) and deported to India on Wednesday, November 19. The CBI, which functions as India’s National Central Bureau for Interpol, secured the RCN at the request of the Kerala Police. The UAE authorities subsequently traced and arrested Rakesh. He had reportedly remained in detention in Dubai for four months after the notice was issued. A chargesheet had already been filed in the case and the court had issued an open-ended arrest warrant against him. A police team from Kerala travelled to Dubai to take custody of the accused and bring him back. The team included Ashwith Karanmayil, Deputy Superintendent of the Thrissur District Crime Branch; Biju Kumar, Sub-Inspector of the Interpol Liaison Wing; and Firoz, a Grade Senior Civil Police Officer attached to Vadanappally Police Station. After his arrival in India, Vadanappally Police Station Sub-Inspector Abin took custody of the accused and completed the necessary legal formalities before formally arresting him. He was subsequently produced before a court and remanded to judicial custody. Murder over previous enmity Dhanesh’s murder took place on October 1, 2008, near the Thirumangalam Temple in Engandiyur. The prosecution case is that the murder was the result of enmity arising from the killing of a man named Sujith. Dhanesh was standing on the roadside talking to a friend when a group of assailants arrived in cars and motorcycles. The attackers, allegedly armed with swords and axes, launched an assault on him. When Dhanesh attempted to escape, the assailants chased him and continued attacking him, inflicting serious injuries. He was rushed to Westfort Hospital in Thrissur, where he died while undergoing treatment. The case involves 11 accused, with the first six allegedly participating directly in the murder. Rakesh was the third accused. The Chavakkad Judicial First Class Magistrate Court had issued a long-pending (LP) warrant against him after he fled abroad. The police filed the chargesheet on December 24, 2009. The case is currently pending before the Thrissur First Additional Sessions Court, where preparations for the trial are nearing completion. The other accused in the case had been arrested earlier. They include Uthaman (51), Ullas (46), Kannan (46), Sajeevan (45), Prathyush (36), Biju (49), Binoj Kumar (52), Manikandan (42) and Gilbish (44). The CBI coordinated the operation with the Ministry of External Affairs, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Kerala Police. The agency also facilitates international police cooperation through BHARATPOL, an online portal developed to help Indian law enforcement agencies coordinate with foreign police forces. According to the CBI, more than 281 wanted criminals have been brought back to India through Interpol channels since 2019, including 73 fugitives in 2026.

articles.title: PM Modi to inaugurate 'Nitish Setu' over Ganga in Bihar on November 21
articles.summary: Patna: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Bihar's Vaishali district on Saturday to inaugurate a Rs 5,500-crore bridge, named after former chief minister Nitish Kumar, over the Ganga, officials said. This would be the prime minister's first visit to the eastern state since May, when he had attended a function marking the expansion of the cabinet headed by Samrat Choudhary, the first BJP leader to lead a government in Bihar. The 9.76-km-long six-lane bridge, which connects Bidupur block in Vaishali to Kachchi Dargah on the outskirts of Patna, has been named 'Nitish Setu', in deference to the former chief minister, on whose watch the project was conceived, and came close to completion. Kumar, who heads the JD(U) and gave up the chief minister's post in April after a nearly two-decade-long tenure, had commissioned the project in 2012, though work began only in 2015, a year after the NDA government at the Centre helped the state borrow money from the Asian Development Bank (ADB), which has lent a total sum of Rs 3.472.15 crore. Naming Ganga bridge as 'Nitish Setu': BJP’s bid to placate miffed JD(U) after MLC poll setback According to the state government, which has spent Rs 2,099.54 crore from its own resources on the project, the bridge, length of which nears 20 km if approach roads on both ends are taken into account, may turn a new leaf in the agrarian economy of densely populated north Bihar. The government expects, as a direct result of the bridge, much easier transportation of litchis, bananas, maize, vegetables and other agricultural produce from north Bihar, which is blessed with fertile soil but saddled with a dense population. The government is also confident that the 'Bidupur-Kachchi Dargah Corridor' will become an attractive destination for investors, as it had the potential of emerging as a hub of tourism and logistics. Besides, traffic congestion on the over 40-year-old Mahatma Gandhi Setu, connecting Patna and Hajipur, is expected to come down after 'Nitish Setu' becomes operational. Meanwhile, naming of the bridge has triggered a war of words between the ruling NDA and the main opposition party RJD, which has shared power with Nitish Kumar, albeit briefly, and seeks to claim its own share of credit. RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav, whose Raghopur assembly segment is set to benefit immensely from the bridge, has alleged that the BJP has sought to declare the JD(U) supremo as "politically dead", by naming the bridge after the leader while he was still alive. Yadav, who is now the leader of the opposition in the state assembly, has also claimed that in 2016, when he was the deputy CM with road construction as one of his portfolios, a proposal had been sent to Nitish Kumar for naming the bridge after Akshayvat Rai, a freedom fighter hailing from Bidupur. The ruling NDA, which enjoys a brute majority in the state assembly, has dismissed the opposition party's objections to the name of the bridge. Those refusing to find fault with the name 'Nitish Setu' include Union minister Chirag Paswan, a former strident critic of the JD(U) supremo, under whose Lok Sabha constituency Hajipur the Raghopur assembly segment falls. Now of the view that the JD(U) supremo deserved the honour, the Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) president responded wistfully when it was pointed out to him that his late father Ram Vilas Paswan, who represented Hajipur several times, too deserved the laurel. "My father was far greater than a bridge or a culvert. His contributions have been acknowledged through government decisions like holding a state function on his birth anniversary. More such honours may come his way in the days to come," Paswan said.

The government said that draft rules for this amendment were previously published in the extraordinary gazette of the government on June 11, 2026, inviting objections and suggestions from affected persons within 30 days. articles.title: Mir Jafar to anti-national — BJP’s politics of silencing criticism
articles.summary: Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi is facing vituperative reactions from members of the Narendra Modi government and the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for his fireside chat at Columbia University, New York. The attack on Gandhi has been unusually aggressive and co-ordinated. He was called a “ part-time politician and full-time peddler of pessimism ” who was working at the behest of “ anti-India forces ”, that he was the “ Mir Jafar of India ”, “immature”, and “irresponsible”. Gandhi did not tell the university audience anything that they did not already know. In the fireside chat moderated by journalist Lydia Polgreen at Columbia University, Gandhi largely reiterated what is already familiar in India’s domestic political discourse and has been reported and reflected upon in international commentary. What has unsettled the government is that he voiced these criticisms before an international audience. His talk wove together unemployment, manufacturing problems, wealth concentrated in a few corporates, a lack of electoral integrity, and democratic discontent into a powerful indictment of India’s economic and political model, questioning its sustainability. Rahul Gandhi 'Mir Jafar' of Indian politics, says BJP's Sambit Patra The definitive formulation that India was “sitting on an economic disaster” , seems to have particularly riled the government and the BJP. It is based on three interconnected concerns: massive unemployment, a deeply troubled education system, and an economy unable to generate adequate opportunities for India’s young population. India’s GDP figures tom-tommed by the government, say little about the quality of employment, labour-force participation, wage levels, or the distribution of economic gains in the population. High growth has not translated into productive employment, rising household incomes, and economic security for all. There is no new revelation in Gandhi’s claim that India has not been able to build a sufficiently strong manufacturing base. It is widely known that the government’s ‘Make in India’ and ‘Startup India’ programmes have not delivered on their promises; that the MSME sector has been weakened , that the services sector alone cannot absorb the increasing number of youngsters entering the labour market and that services cannot replace manufacturing as the main job provider in India. The BJP could legitimately ask Gandhi what alternative strategy he would pursue to generate employment in manufacturing as China’s industrialisation was able to do. But calling him “Mir Jafar” is hardly a fruitful rebuttal. The most consequential economic question that Gandhi asked was: “Why is there no private investment in India? Why are the only people who are growing in India called Adani and Ambani?” Concentration of wealth and crony capitalism under the Modi regime is nothing new and has attracted considerable international attention . By linking the two, Gandhi was pointing to the lack of a level playing field and fair competition. International investors have legitimate concerns about an economic structure where investment, infrastructure, finance, and the strategic sector are dominated by a handful of corporates. Airports, forest land, defence contracts , and even established hotels have been given to or bought over by the government’s ‘ favourite capitalists ’. The most consequential political issue that Gandhi raised at Columbia University was about 13.3 crore voters being removed from the rolls used in the 2024 general elections. His argument in public in Delhi and repeated in Columbia has been that even if roughly 15% of those who voted in 2024 had their names removed from the SIR which followed the general elections, the legitimacy of the polls themselves would be questionable — as the margin of difference between the vote shares of the BJP-led NDA and the I.N.D.I.A. bloc was roughly 3%. For months now, these allegations have been central to Gandhi’s ‘vote-theft’ campaign. One can question whether the 13.3 crore disenfranchised, were in fact legitimately removed as deceased or duplicated, but the question itself about electoral integrity cannot be dismissed as ‘anti-national’. Gandhi’s talk about youth protests as a global phenomenon is hardly new to an international audience. His larger argument was that the global economic system is unable to meet the aspirations of the young or offer them a credible future. India’s youth protests were placed in this context. He also suggested that educated, middle class families that were previously enamoured of Modi were becoming disillusioned. Gandhi claimed that students, farmers, and others, including bloggers, had lost their earlier inhibitions against questioning the government for fear of repressive measures. The July youth protests and subsequent memes mocking Modi suggest that the once unassailable public image is weakened and resistance is loud and visible . Gandhi’s assertion that democracy in India is a global public good is once again not new. India’s democratic experiment, secularism, size, and diversity have been a subject of international political and academic interest. By invoking the international movement for democracy, Gandhi has projected the Opposition’s struggle against the Modi regime not merely as an attempt at electoral victory but as a commitment to the restoration of independent democratic institutions, promoting secularism, and tolerance of diversity, fostering an independent press, and protecting civil liberties. As the Leader of the Opposition in the world’s largest democracy, he is well within his right to address a global audience on these issues. The Modi government’s misuse of investigative agencies, intolerance of civil society voices, pressure on independent journalists, police brutality against protestors, and the erosion of independence of democratic institutions has been noted by several international human rights, press freedom organisations, and other global commentators. They do not need Gandhi to inform them of these developments. These familiar criticisms, when repeated on foreign soil by the Leader of the Opposition, acquire greater significance for the BJP. Because the party conflates the Modi government with the nation it sees criticism in international forums as a question of national loyalty. This is quite apart from the fact that the international image which the prime minister had deeply invested in since his first term, has been falling apart even without Gandhi’s criticism. The BJP’s vitriolic reactions focus on undermining the personal credibility of the critic. articles.title: Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu's pleas seeking release of 11 TMC water from Cauvery river
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed Tamil Nadu's pleas seeking direction to Karnataka government for releasing 11 TMC of water from Cauvery river. A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Aparesh Singh said Tamil Nadu has filed a third application for bringing on record some additional documents, which will also be dismissed. The Tamil Nadu government had filed two petitions seeking directions for the immediate release of its due share of Cauvery water. The Karnataka government had told the top court that it would be difficult to meet Tamil Nadu's demand for the release of 11 TMC feet of Cauvery river water for making good a "shortfall" as this was a rain-deficit year and several areas have been declared drought-affected. Tamil Nadu, in August had alleged that it had not received its allocated share from Karnataka despite facing a rain-deficient year. It submitted that due to a shortfall of about 11 thousand million cubic feet (TMC), it was unable to supply any water for irrigation. Karnataka government, however, denied the claims and stated that it had complied with the orders of the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA).

articles.summary: Washington: A teenager accused of planning a mass shootout at a Hindu temple near Chicago pleaded not guilty to all charges in a US court, local media reported. Alexandros Paporakis, 19, who made a failed bid for a mass shootout at a temple in Aurora, Illinois, was indicted on one count each of making a terrorist threat and unlawful use of a weapon, CBS News reported. Paporakis appeared before Cook County judge Marc Martin at the Rolling Meadows Third Municipal District courthouse on Thursday, the Daily Herald reported. Paporakis was initially charged with making a terrorist threat and unlawful use of a weapon in connection with the alleged plot at the Sri Venkateswara Temple in Aurora. articles.title: Destination Cabinet Meeting to be Held at Gandhi Sagar Dam Site
articles.summary: Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said that the State Government has been organising Destination Cabinet meetings at different locations across Madhya Pradesh to highlight their heritage, geographical features and potential. He also informed that on Tuesday, he would inaugurate and dedicate various development works in the Manasa Assembly constituency of Neemuch district. The Chief Minister shared this information while interacting with the media at the Chief Minister's Residence on Tuesday, before leaving for the Destination Cabinet meeting at Gandhi Sagar. Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said that hydropower plants and pumped hydro storage represent new technologies in the field of electricity generation. The Gandhi Sagar Pumped Hydro Storage Project is being developed at a cost of ₹11,474 crore. Once operational, it will generate 2,000 MW of electricity during peak demand hours, enabling an immediate supply of power as per requirements. This will ensure adequate electricity availability in the state round the clock. The cost of electricity generated through this project is also expected to be nearly half that of conventional sources. The Gandhi Sagar Pumped Hydro Storage Project is not only the first of its kind in India but also across the entire Asian continent. Chief Minister Dr. Yadav described it as a major leap forward for Madhya Pradesh in power generation. Following its inauguration, school and college students as well as research scholars will be brought here on educational visits to understand how electricity is generated through this technology. Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi consistently encourages innovation and public welfare initiatives. In this context, the project, which generates electricity using water, will be no less than a pilgrimage site for those interested in science. Madhya Pradesh is an extraordinary centre of natural resources and tourism potential. The Chief Minister said that the cheetah reintroduction project at Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary is also progressing successfully. The region is home to prehistoric inscriptions and rock paintings on rocks and stone formations dating back thousands and even millions of years. Gandhi Sagar is an important centre of tribal culture, ancient archaeological heritage, water resources and tourism. Located in the western part of Madhya Pradesh, along the Rajasthan border, the Gandhi Sagar Dam region is also providing livelihood and income opportunities to a large number of members of the fishing community through cage culture technology. Destination Cabinet Meetings Held Outside Bhopal · January 3, 2024: The State Cabinet meeting was held at Shakti Bhawan in Jabalpur. · October 5, 2024: A Cabinet meeting was held at Singrampur in Damoh district in honour of Veerangana Rani Durgavati. · January 24, 2025: The Cabinet meeting was held in Maheshwar, district Khargone, the city of Lokmata Ahilyabai. · May 20, 2025: A Cabinet meeting was held at Rajwada in Indore to mark the 300th birth anniversary of Lokmata Devi Ahilyabai Holkar. · June 3, 2025: A Cabinet meeting dedicated to the valour of Gond King Bhabhut Singh was held at Raj Bhavan in Pachmarhi, Narmadapuram district. · December 9, 2025: A Cabinet meeting was held at the Maharaja Chhatrasal Convention Centre in Khajuraho in honour of the Bundelkhand region. · March 2, 2026: The Cabinet meeting was held at the Bhilat Baba temple in Nagalwadi, a tribal-dominated area of Barwani district. · July 19, 2026: A Cabinet meeting was held at Jagdishpur village in Bhopal district, home to the historic palace and memorial associated with Gond Queen Rani Kamlapati. Gandhi Sagar Pumped Hydro Storage Project: Asia's Largest Project The 1,920 MW Gandhi Sagar Pumped Hydro Storage Project, being developed by Greenko Group at Gandhi Sagar in Neemuch district, involves an investment of approximately ₹11,500 crore. Spread over an area of around 414 hectares in Khemala Block of Rampura Tehsil, it is the largest standalone pumped hydro storage project under construction in India and Asia. Once completed, the project will be capable of generating electricity at its full capacity of 1,920 MW continuously for six hours. The project comprises two reservoirs, with the existing Gandhi Sagar Reservoir, having a total capacity of approximately 270 TMC (7,643.70 MCM), serving as the lower reservoir. Only 2.4 TMC (67.66 MCM) of water will be utilised on a non-consumptive basis, meaning that it will not be consumed but repeatedly recycled and reused through a closed-loop system. Under the pumping mode, surplus solar or wind energy available from the grid during the day or night will be used to operate reversible motor-pump units, which will pump water from the lower reservoir to the upper reservoir for storage. During peak demand hours, water will be released from the upper reservoir into the lower reservoir, driving the reversible units in the opposite direction to operate as turbines and generate electricity for supply to the grid. The project will have a rated head of approximately 122 metres in turbine mode and an estimated round-trip efficiency of around 80 per cent, which means that nearly 80 per cent of the energy used for pumping can be recovered during power generation. A total of nine turbines are being installed, with an estimated annual electricity generation capacity of 3,580 million units (MU), equivalent to 3,580 million kWh. The project is connected to the 765/400 kV PGCIL/CTU substation in Mandsaur district, approximately 60 km away, for pumping operations and evacuation of generated electricity. The first set of turbines is scheduled to become operational in December 2026, while commercial operations of the entire project are expected to commence in June 2027. During the construction phase, the project has provided employment to approximately 4,000 people. Its operation and maintenance are expected to generate around 200 permanent jobs.

articles.title: Powering Chhattisgarh's Growth: Shri Modi's Vision, Shri Sai's Action
articles.summary: From record paddy procurement and expanding infrastructure to women's economic empowerment and the transition towards peace, Chhattisgarh's development journey reflects the convergence of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 and Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai's governance priorities. Building on Central schemes and assistance, the state is pursuing investment-led growth, strengthening public services and extending development opportunities to remote and tribal communities. Over the past 12 years, Chhattisgarh has received ₹3,46,806 crore as its share of Central taxes, around 7.4 times the ₹47,100 crore received between 2004 and 2014. The District Mineral Foundation has contributed ₹17,887 crore towards more than 81,000 development works. "Our vision is to make Viksit Chhattisgarh a strong foundation for Viksit Bharat 2047. Through the 'Chhattisgarh Anjor Vision 2047' roadmap, we are harnessing our mineral and energy resources, farmers, youth, women's empowerment and rich tribal heritage to build a prosperous, secure and self-reliant state," said Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai, reaffirming his commitment to the Prime Minister's principles of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas'. Inspired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's tenure as Gujarat Chief Minister, Chhattisgarh has initiated more than 450 structural and policy reforms, including public dialogue initiatives such as 'Chintan Shivir'. Among the major reforms, the Ease of Doing Business Act, 2026 provides for deemed approvals, while 279 minor offences have been decriminalised through amendments under the Jan Vishwas Acts. Together with the New Industrial Policy, these measures have helped attract investment proposals worth ₹8.50 lakh crore, with potential to generate over 1.60 lakh jobs. On the infrastructure front, national highway projects worth ₹35,766 crore have been sanctioned, including 37 projects worth ₹18,215 crore under implementation. Railway expansion worth an estimated ₹54,000 crore is underway, and the six-lane Raipur–Visakhapatnam Expressway, when completed, will strengthen connectivity with ports and international trade routes. On the power front, the Lara Super Thermal Power Project's capacity has expanded from 4,000 MW to 4,800 MW, and the state has also received energy investment proposals worth approximately ₹3.5 lakh crore. Under PMAY, over 11.78 lakh houses have been constructed in the two years and nine months of Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai's tenure. Swachh Bharat Abhiyan supported 36 lakh household toilets and 14,970 community toilets, with ₹2,437 crore in Central assistance. Mahtari Vandan Yojana provides ₹1,000 monthly to 68 lakh women, while nearly 14 lakh women have become Lakhpati Didis. Under BIHAN, 32.39 lakh rural families are associated with 2.98 lakh self-help groups, and over 70,000 tribal women are linked to Van Dhan Vikas Kendras. AgriStack has generated 42 lakh Farmer IDs, while SVAMITVA has provided property records to 7.51 lakh rural residents. The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana provided free LPG connections to 39.73 lakh women. Healthcare schemes enabled 51.17 lakh beneficiaries to receive treatment worth ₹11,877 crore, while Ayushman Bharat covers 2.49 crore people. Under PMGKAY and Mukhyamantri Khadyan Sahayata Yojana, 73 lakh families (1.99 crore people) receive free ration, backed by ₹5,600 crore in Central-scheme subsidy. PM-KISAN benefited 26.57 lakh farmers through direct transfers. Registered farmers increased from 13.17 lakh in 2015 to 27.53 lakh, while registered agricultural area expanded from 21.26 lakh to 33 lakh hectares. Paddy procurement rose from 59 lakh to a record 141 lakh metric tonnes, with ₹33,431 crore paid as MSP and ₹10,292 crore as bonuses. The Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan targets infrastructure development in over 6,000 tribal-dominated villages. PM-JANMAN has extended housing, roads and drinking water to over 56,000 families from five PVTGs across 18 districts. Rising demand for millets (Shri Anna) is also opening market opportunities for tribal farmers cultivating kodo, kutki and ragi in Bastar and Surguja. As Chhattisgarh accelerates its development push, Bastar remains central to the agenda. March 31, 2026, marked a decisive milestone in the coordinated efforts of the Centre, the state and security forces to eliminate Naxalism. The restoration of normalcy has enabled 421 schools, shut for years due to violence, to reopen. Complementing these gains, the Niyad Nella Nar Yojana is extending healthcare, education, ration and other essential public services to remote villages, translating improved security into renewed opportunities for inclusive development.

articles.title: Supreme Court limits High Court interference in religious trusts, restores trial court orders
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has underlined the narrow scope of High Court supervision under Article 227 of the Constitution in interim management of religious and charitable institutions, ruling that representative suits under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure do not give every interested person an automatic right to join the proceedings. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh set aside interim and subsequent orders of the Calcutta High Court that had disrupted arrangements made by a trial court for the interim administration of Sri Guru Sangha, a charitable society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860. The apex court restored the trial court’s orders constituting a 13-member ad hoc committee and rejecting certain impleadment applications. Supreme Court orders counselling for 6-year-old after finding father tutored in violation of order In its judgment on November 19, 2026, the court reiterated that supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 is not meant to correct every error of fact or law, nor does it allow a High Court to replace the subordinate court’s conclusions with its own. Interference is justified only in cases of patent jurisdictional error, perversity or grave miscarriage of justice. Relying on its earlier decision in M/s Garment Craft Vs Prakash Chand Goel (2022), the bench held that the High Court’s intervention was unwarranted. The appellants, members of the Sangha and plaintiffs in a title suit filed under Section 92 CPC, had sought removal of certain office-bearers, framing of a scheme of management and appointment of a receiver. The Sangha’s central ashram is in Kolkata. During the suit’s pendency, the trial court first appointed a special officer and later, on a joint application of the parties, constituted the 13-member ad hoc committee on June 7, 2022, with directions for quarterly reports and annual audits. The High Court stayed that arrangement and later set aside the trial court’s rejection of impleadment pleas, observing that the suit was representative in nature. Meritorious case eclipsed by form: Supreme Court steps in for school clerks after 20-year ordeal The Supreme Court disagreed. It held that while a Section 92 suit concerns the interests of persons associated with the institution, applicants must still satisfy Order I Rule 10(2) CPC by showing that their presence is necessary or proper for complete adjudication. General allegations of mismanagement and mere association with the society are not enough. The bench noted that the trial court had called for and considered the special officer’s explanation before removing her and forming the committee. The High Court had proceeded on the incorrect premise that she was denied a hearing. The court found no perversity or legal infirmity in the trial court’s reasoned orders was demonstrated. It said allegations of financial and administrative irregularities against the ad hoc committee involved disputed questions that the trial court, which continued to seize of the suit, was competent to examine. The Supreme Court declined to appoint a fresh committee or independent administrator at this stage and left parties free to raise grievances before the trial court. No objection if ex-SC judge acts as mediator in Krishna-Godavari basin gas migration dispute: Centre to Supreme Court The civil appeals were allowed. The High Court’s orders of September 26, 2022 and February 4, 2026 were set aside. The trial court’s June 7, 2022 order remains operative, subject to further directions by the competent court. The September 9, 2025 rejection of impleadment applications by Bachhu Ranjan Das and Bablu Das was restored. Pending revisional proceedings before the High Court would be decided on their own merits, uninfluenced by the present judgment. The trial court was directed to proceed independently with the suit and all pending applications.

articles.title: Advocate flags media sensationalism in Bilkis Bano appeals, denies suppression
articles.summary: New Delhi: An advocate representing two convicts in the Bilkis Bano case has criticised attempts to sensationalise pending Supreme Court proceedings, calling claims that the prosecutrix was kept in the dark “false and only meant for publicity”. Ayush Anand, Advocate-on-Record for Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi alias Lala Doctor and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya, who were granted bail, issued a statement. “Ideally an advocate should not issue any press brief for his sub-judice matter. But as some misleading statement has been issued and that too by a senior advocate directly on behalf of the prosecutrix which is not only factually incorrect but to sensationalise the Court proceedings in this matter and doubting the sanctity of the legal process this statement is being issued to put things in the correct perspective,” he said. Bilkis Bano case: Two convicts get bail from Supreme Court after being in jail for 17 years Anand said his clients “not being the main accused were alleged for being in mob and not even named for any overt act initially.” He noted that the prosecutrix’s statements dated March 7 and 13, 2002, “has not named my clients for allegation of rape. Similar was her statement before the doctor at the time of medical examination.” The special leave petitions were filed on August 15, 2025. The matter was listed four times before a bench issued notice on March 17, 2026, after considering the petitioners’ prolonged incarceration of about 17 years and the physical disability of one of them. “When notice has been issued in this matter on 17.03.2026, this was also reported in a major media outlet. So, the allegation that prosecutrix was not aware is false,” Anand said. He pointed out that no caveat was filed on behalf of the prosecutrix and she was not a party before the high court. “Their failure to act cannot be put against my client or the court suggesting motives," he said. After notice, the appeals were listed four more times. On medical grounds— petitioner No. 1 suffered critical cardiac condition with multiple blockages and underwent major procedures — the court granted bail on October 28, 2026, following detailed hearing. ‘Will fight this order’: Shocked and scared Bilkis Bano says will appeal against bail granted to two rape convicts “This matter was put up for hearing for 10 times before granting bail to my clients and took more than a year, hence alleging suppression… is completely mischievous,” the statement said. Anand cited the Supreme Court’s practice of granting bail after long incarceration, referring to recent orders in other criminal appeals where bail was given after 12 and 18 years behind bars. From November 16, 2026 — 18 days after the bail order — “suddenly this issue is being coloured in a fashion that prosecutrix is apparently shocked to know this. This smear media campaign before seeking appropriate legal remedy is a sharp practice and unfortunately joined by senior counsel without verifying the facts,” he said. “Getting personal publicity out of a case does not behoves any lawyer or officer of the court or litigant,” Anand added, urging that sensationalisation of court proceedings in a sub-judice matter on presumption should be avoided.

The Hindu reported that senior Defence Ministry officials said the figures published in the directory did not originate from the IAF. articles.summary: Ottawa: The Canadian Police have added Satinderjeet Singh alias Goldy Brar to their wanted list in connection with the 2023 killing of an alleged member of a rival gang in Winnipeg, according to local media reports. Brar, 32, is wanted on charges of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder, CBC News reported on Thursday. He is also suspected to have been "instrumental" in a wide range of crimes across Canada, it said, quoting the police. FBI puts gangster Goldy Brar on 10 most wanted list with $1 million reward Separately, Brar topped Canada's list of 25 most-wanted fugitives released on Thursday by the BOLO Programme, a private, non-profit public-safety initiative that cooperates with Canadian police services. It offers a reward of up to 250,000 Canadian dollars for any information leading to his arrest in Canada or the United States. According to CBC News , Winnipeg Police are seeking Brar in connection with the killing of Sukhdool Singh Gill, 39, alias Sukha Duneke, whose body was found at a home on Hazelton Drive in northwest Winnipeg on September 20, 2023, after police responded to reports of a shooting. Gill was allegedly involved in a longstanding feud with rival gangs in India and had been accused of extortion and sending money to gang associates in the country, it said. Police are also seeking Brar in connection with two more murders, including the 2023 assassination of Khalistan separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in British Columbia. Brar, who left India for Canada on a student visa in 2017 and belongs to Sri Muktsar Sahib district in Punjab, was a trusted member of the Bishnoi gang. Indian officials believe he is part of the Brar-Rohit Godara-Kala Jatheri gang. Brar was among the fugitives identified following Operation Hardball, a years-long federal investigation into India-based transnational organised crime groups. Brar is named in 52 FIRs registered at different places in Punjab. The Punjab government has also announced a reward of Rs 10 lakh for those providing credible information leading to his arrest. The gangster, who already had an Interpol Red Corner Notice against him, was designated an "individual terrorist" by India in 2024 under the stringent Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). articles.title: Chennai: 70 kg heroin worth Rs 700 crore seized from ice cream vending vehicle
articles.summary: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) seized around 70 kg of heroin, worth Rs 700 crore in the international market, from an ice cream vending vehicle near Madhavaram in Chennai on Tuesday, November 17. Two men have been arrested in connection with the seizure and remanded to judicial custody. The accused have been identified as Abdul Shukkur (32) and Shafiq Ahmed (30), both natives of southern Tamil Nadu who were residing in Chennai. According to reports, the DRI received specific intelligence inputs on Monday night about a large consignment of narcotics being smuggled from abroad and being transported through vehicles in Chennai suburbs. Following the tip-off, special teams were formed and surveillance was intensified near Chennai airport and along the Chennai-Tiruchy and Chennai-Kolkata National Highways. On Tuesday, DRI officials spotted an ice cream vending vehicle parked near an ice manufacturing factory in Madhavaram, along the Chennai-Kolkata National Highway. articles.title: My teen wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6. What do I need to know about the game?
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6, more commonly known as GTA6, is released on Thursday . I can’t wait to play. Neither can my 13-year-old. They’ve watched the trailers and the Netflix extended look . Their friends are talking about it. So are popular YouTube streamers. It’s easy to understand why they want to join in. What’s the game about? GTA6 follows the characters Jason and Lucia – a couple caught up in a criminal conspiracy. Think of a crime drama you can take part in. Game developer Rockstar’s character descriptions mention drug trafficking, prison and a strip club financed by drug money. It’s an open-world game, meaning players can explore activities between story missions . For players, that freedom is part of the appeal. But current trailers and game play videos reveal little about the surrounding story lines. Earlier games in the series show the range of adult content commonly featured. For example, GTA San Andreas , released in 2004, depicts paid sexual encounters and drug use. And GTA5, which came out in 2013, included a torture mission that made players carry out the violence. While these examples don’t tell us exactly what happens in GTA6, they explain why we need to look beyond the trailers. Can teens still get access? We know in Australia R18+ games are legally restricted to adults . For GTA6, the classification entry lists “high impact violence, sex scenes and drug use”. This gives parents something specific to discuss with their teenager if they express interest in playing. In March, Australia’s new online safety codes came into effect. As part of these codes, online gaming platforms must now require players to provide age assurance to allow them to access R18+ content. This means gaming companies PlayStation and Xbox (consoles GTA6 is available on) now require age checks for the game through their Australian stores. Worried about your child playing anyway? Checking who buys a game doesn’t decide who holds the controller afterwards. Teenagers could still play on an adult’s account. You can create a separate user account for your teenager and set age restrictions through PlayStation Family or Xbox Family Settings . If you’re planning to play the game yourself, you can protect adult accounts with a login passcode, too. Be aware if you decide not to let your teen play, they might still encounter the game on an older sibling’s account or at a friend’s house. Survey data, published in 2023 , estimated around 70% of GTA gamers in Britain first played the game when they were under 18. Jason and Lucia are the main characters at the centre of Grand Theft Auto 6’s crime story. Do violent video games encourage teens’ bad behaviour? While some studies have suggested there is a small link between violent gaming and later physical aggression in children and teenagers, the larger body of research doesn’t support such a correlation. The American Psychological Association has acknowledged this, saying there’s not enough evidence to link violent games with violent behaviour in players. However, parents should not ignore the game’s inclusion of strong impact nudity and sexual content. While a 2020 study found there wasn’t enough evidence to link sexualised content in games with increased sexist attitudes in players, previous GTA games have been criticised for being misogynistic and sexist. Is watching different from playing? Over the past decade, there has been a surge in watching other people play video games – much like you would watch TV or a film. This online streaming of gameplay is often mixed with commentary, humour and editing. A US study, published in March , examined livestreams on Twitch (an online platform popular for streaming gameplay). The study found aggressive speech from streamers was linked with more aggressive chat messages posted by viewers. But violent gameplay itself showed no significant association with aggressive chat messages. However, the study did not establish causation or effects specifically on teenagers. The findings cannot tell us whether watching a game is safer than playing it. Both can potentially expose a teenager to an age-inappropriate content. So what do I tell my teen? When it comes to choosing games with your children, the eSafety Commissioner recommends : checking game classifications and reviews discussing boundaries, such as what types of content are OK and what aren’t (and why) making rules about when a game can be played and in which rooms of the home encouraging children to speak up when something makes them uncomfortable. It’s also important to include watching gameplay videos and visits to friends’ houses as part of conversations about gaming. If the answer ends up being “no”, experts say parents should acknowledge and validate teenagers’ feelings, especially if they react strongly to the decision. So when it comes to my 13-year-old child, I am explaining how scenes in the game are not suitable for them without dismissing their interest in it. And if they encounter something inappropriate through a friend or an online video, I want them to feel they can tell me, even when I’ve said no to the game. articles.title: Ariyil Shukkoor murder: 13 found guilty; CPI(M) leaders Jayarajan, Rajesh acquitted
articles.summary: Eighteen accused, including senior leaders of Communist Party of India (Marxist) P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh, were acquitted in the murder case of Ariyil Shukkoor, a member of the Muslim Students Federation (MSF). A special CBI court in Kochi on Thursday, November 19, found 13 persons guilty in the case. The quantum of the sentence will be pronounced at 3 PM. Shukkoor, 24, was murdered on February 20, 2012 by a vigilante mob, following an attack on the vehicle used by Jayarajan and Rajesh to visit Pattuvam in Kannur during a League-CPI(M) conflict. Jayarajan, then Kannur district secretary of CPI(M) and Rajesh, then an MLA, were accused of conspiracy in the murder. According to reports, Shukkoor was subjected to a ‘Kangaroo court’ trial for around two hours by the CPI(M) workers before he was stabbed to death. Special judge CBI-III (Ernakulam) P Sabarinathan found accused Sumesh KV, Anoop, Pavithran P, Manoharan PV, NP Ajith Kumar, P P Suresan, EP Radhakrishnan, Shijin Mohan @ Shijin, KV Sajith, VV Mohanan, Purushothaman MV @ Purushu, P K Ajith Kumar, and P P Suresan as guilty. Two accused passed away during trial. ‘Acquittal not on merit’: Special Prosecutor As per the case, Jayarajan and Rajesh, the 32nd and 33rd accused, were aware that Shukkoor was in the custody of CPI(M) workers and did nothing to prevent the murder. Both were charged with Section 118 of the Indian Penal Code (concealing a design to commit an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life). Special prosecutor K Padmanaban said that two crucial witnesses in the case refused to turn up for the trial. “The acquittals of 32nd and 33nd accused were not on merit. They were acquitted only because witnesses were not examined at the court. The 22nd and 23 witnesses refused to attend the trial. One witness is abroad. CBI served multiple notices for the second witness, but he remained absconding. The Kerala society must ask why this happened,” he said. Prosecution lawyers said that they are not satisfied, especially regarding the acquittal of second accused Ganesh. “As per the postmortem report, A1 (accused 1) stabbed on chest and A2 (accused 2) on stomach. Those two were fatal injuries. The weapon used by the accused, which was recovered following his confession, was produced in the court. There were blood stains on the weapon. An appeal will be filed against acquittal of the second accused,” lawyers said. Shyamjith, son of CPI(M) state general secretary MV Govindan, who was the 19th accused, too was acquitted. Speaking to the media after the verdict, Jayarajan alleged that the case was framed by League leadership to cause a mistrust among the minority community towards the CPI(M) leaders. Jayarajan said that a former Indian Police Service officer, who later joined the BJP, was behind adding section 118 against him and Rajesh. Jayarajan also alleged that a former judge of Kerala High Court took a biased stand. Rajesh asked why prosecution failed to bring the witnesses to court. “It is a politically fabricated case,” he said. CPI(M) Kannur district secretary K K Ragesh said the allegation of a CPI(M) kangaroo court was a media creation. State industries minister and Indian Union Muslim league general secretary PK Kunhalikutty said that there was no doubt that Shukkoor murder was a planned one. “Everyone knows that the witness failed to appear before the court due to fear. An appeal should be filed to prove the conspiracy angle,” he said.
